title: How Pieter Levels builds MVPs fast: rough, minimal, own-stack shipping
summary: Levels explains his 12-startups workflow: solve your own problems, keep sites minimal, own the whole stack on one cheap VPS, skip frameworks and databases, and deploy a new site in about 15 minutes. His core message is that tools matter less than being fast and comfortable with what you know.

principles.text: Start by solving your own problems; it's a great way to begin, even if you later aim for a wider audience.
principles.quote: It’s great to start off by solving your own problems.

principles.text: Build minimal on purpose; don't build big immediately or stuff a site with functionality.
principles.quote: I don’t have as much as time to build things big and I don’t see the point of building things big immediately.

principles.text: Work fast and rough rather than longer hours; speed comes from workflow, not hours.
principles.quote: I don’t work particularly longer hours than most people (I think). I do work fast and rough.

principles.text: Avoid frameworks that add complexity; keep code simple and reuse code from previous projects.
principles.quote: Except for jQuery, I don’t use any frameworks. Why? Because many times, they just make things more complex.

principles.text: Own the whole stack on one simple, cheap server so you can debug quickly and deploy in minutes.
principles.quote: I now owned the entire stack. From front-end, back-end to the server itself.

principles.text: Use plain JSON files instead of a database at small scale; migrate to a real database later if needed.
principles.quote: You can always write a script that puts this in a MySQL/MariaDB/PostgreSQL database later.
